title.narrative: Sanivation Regional Expansion

description.narrative: Sanivation partners with local governments to enable waste to be safely managed. To date, in Kenya, Sanivation has partnered with local governments to leverage >$10M in infrastructure funding for sanitation, reach >100,000 people, and created systemic change with national government through policy change and creation of national targets for city-wide inclusive sanitation. Sanivation is now using learnings from Kenya to expand (and respond to requests to expand) to new countries. Through this support, they will deliver on and derisk their developed regional expansion plan, growing their impact!

_Calculate Net profit Margin as a Percentage: Net Profit margin = Net Profit ⁄ Total revenue x 100. Net profit is calculated by deducting all company expenses from its total revenue. The result of the profit margin calculation is a percentage – for example, a 10% profit margin means for each $1 of revenue the company earns $0.10 in net profit. Revenue represents the total sales of the company in a period. Calculate over minimum of 6 months._

comment.narrative: 07-01-2025: As part of our market strategy, we identified Nigeria and Tanzania as focus countries for expansion. Leveraging our market approach—delivering projects on a fee-for-service basis or co-developing projects with governments and mandate holders—we aim to sustain profit margins of 30-40%. This is evidenced by the two projects already secured in Nigeria. Looking ahead, we are positioning ourselves to begin operating FSTPs by 2027, further solidifying our long-term operational goals and market presence.

title.narrative: Other indicators (P) and narrative explanation
Please provide a short narrative explanation of the data here. (max 250 words)

actual.value:
Sanivation has made significant progress aligned with Aqua for All's impact measures, demonstrating our commitment to sustainable water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) solutions in Africa. We've created 55 jobs, exceeding our goal of 52, with a 17% increase in female employment, highlighting our focus on inclusivity and gender equity.
Our Regional Expansion initiative combines local and imported resources through strategic partnerships, addressing sourcing challenges. Collaborating with both local and non-local teams for facility maintenance ensures long-term sustainability. We’ve seen substantial stakeholder engagement, with support in Zambia and active efforts in Nigeria and Tanzania. In Nigeria, we offer technical assistance to state governments, while in Tanzania, partnerships with organizations like SUEZ position us as a long-term provider of onsite sanitation solutions.
Market assessments in Ethiopia, Tanzania, Zambia, and Nigeria show a clear demand for affordable resource recovery solutions, aligning our efforts with local needs. We are also connecting our plans with funding opportunities through engagement with institutions like the World Bank and African Development Bank.Collaborations with organizations such as ICE, UNICEF, WaterAid, and local networks like Bread of Life Foundation enhance our project development and integrate our work into communities. Political stability and positive economic conditions in our priority areas further support our operations.
By leveraging local expertise, strategic partnerships, and strong stakeholder engagement, Sanivation is established as a leader in delivering effective and sustainable sanitation solutions, ensuring a lasting impact in the region.
